subject: Deployment mode pricing breakdown and next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode pricing breakdown and next steps

Hi Emma -

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the pricing breakdown we promised for the three deployment modes (hosted API / dedicated capacity / private VPC):

- Hosted API: best for quick time-to-value. Per-token pricing, no infra commits. Good for variable traffic and proof-of-concepts.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools; monthly committed spend. Predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at steady-state.
- Private VPC (on-prem option): enterprise deployment with platform fee + optional support. Higher upfront/annual costs; necessary for regulated data.

Attached is a templated estimate with example usage profiles (P50 and P90) and a side-by-side cost model. Key follow-ups we discussed:
1) Confirm target QPS and average sequence length for your NLU/assistant workloads (you mentioned ~80 qps and ~120 tokens avg).
2) Clarify data residency & audit needs (SOC2 + retention window).
3) Procurement timeline / PO requirements - Laura I copied for procurement coordination.

Next steps: if you can confirm the two items above, I'll update the estimate for a Dedicated commit vs Hosted per-token comparison showing break-even points.

Attachment: Acme-RI-Estimate-2026-03.pdf (PDF, 45KB)

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@acme-analytics.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode pricing breakdown and next steps

Thanks Aditya - really helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Target throughput: our baseline is 80 qps but we expect bursts to 200 qps during end-of-month reporting windows.
- Avg tokens: ~120 outbound tokens per request; prompt size varies but P50 ~300 tokens total context.
- Compliance: SOC2 required, and we need the option for data to be confined to our VPC for some sensitive pipelines (so Private VPC is on the table for those).

Procurement: we generally need a SOW + PO; procurement team will confirm exact PO cadence. Can Laura loop in on SLAs and contract language?

If you can send the Dedicated vs Hosted cost breakeven with the burst profile included, that would be ideal.

- Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Product, Acme Analytics
emma.liu@acme-analytics.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode pricing breakdown and next steps

Emma - great, thanks for confirming those numbers. I updated the attached estimate to include:

- Two usage scenarios: steady-state (80 qps) and burst windows (200 qps for ~4 hours/day).
- Per-token hosted pricing (list rates) vs Dedicated reserved capacity monthly commit (GPU-hour equivalent) and a modeled break-even at ~110 qps steady-state.
- Private VPC: line items for platform license, installation support, and annual support SLA add-on.

High-level takeaways from the model (see page 2 of the PDF):
- If Acme expects sustained >110 qps for core traffic, Dedicated reserved capacity delivers ~30-40% lower unit cost versus Hosted.
- If most workload is intermittent with short bursts, Hosted with autoscale and caching will likely be more cost-effective initially.
- Private VPC is competitively priced at scale but has onboarding and O&M costs - recommended only for regulated pipelines or where VPC isolation is contractually required.

Action items:
- Laura: can you confirm typical contract language for Dedicated commits and the standard SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted?
- Emma: once procurement confirms PO timing, we can draft a 60-day pilot on Hosted (to validate traffic and caching effects) with an optional conversion to Dedicated commit at month 3.

Attachment: Acme-RI-Estimate-2026-03.pdf (updated)

Thanks - I'll follow up with a one-page decision matrix.

Best,
Aditya
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Emma Liu <emma.liu@acme-analytics.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode pricing breakdown and next steps

Quick note from procurement/contracting side -

- Dedicated commits: standard term is 12 months with monthly billing and a minimum 3-month ramp. We do offer quarterly true-up windows for changes in committed capacity.
- SLA: Dedicated customers get a 99.9% uptime SLA; Hosted has an operational SLA but no capacity reservation guarantees.
- PO requirements: Acme can send a PO referencing the SOW. I can prepare an SOW draft once Emma confirms the pilot scope (recommended: 60-day Hosted pilot covering the two primary endpoints).

Laura Bennett
Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
